prompt:
Design an expressive iOS/macOS Travel Time widget for a desktop dashboard, estimating commute to the next event. Generate 5 distinct compositions in Small (160x160), Medium (340x160) and Large (340x340). One layout per size, rendered once. No repeats.

Compositions (distinct surfaces, palettes & motion):
1 Split-Flap Map: White (#FFFFFF) card; top inset pastel map with pulsing blue radar dot and route line; bottom pairs huge "29 mins" left with grey split-flap boxes ("3" "7") right + event name.
2 Route Nodes: White card with soft top map fade + gliding car graphic, bold "12 min until arrival", dashed route line ("o---o---o") with blue nodes, and grey route pill badge.
3 Mode Stepper: White card with destination header, horizontal stepper of connected orange circles with white mode icons (Drive, Transit, Walk) + pulsing ring.
4 Night Scrim: Full-bleed dark street backdrop with drifting light streaks, white event header at top, bright yellow "18 mins" bottom-left, white pill bar right.
5 Cobalt Stack: Vibrant blue (#0A7AFF) card with gradient sweep; 3 rows (Drive, Transit, Walk) with left icons, traffic note, and bold right minutes.

Hard content limits per size:
Small: travel minutes or leave-by hero, event name, plus ONE item (node line, badge, or bar). Max 3 items. No mode list.
Medium: Small's content plus ONE block: top inset map, 3-mode orange circle stepper, or split-flap boxes + traffic.
Large: Medium's content plus ONE more block: full 3-mode comparison (Drive, Transit, Walk) + buffer.
Never squeeze larger content into a smaller size.

Spacing & Visual: 24px squircle; padding 16px Small, 20px Medium/Large; 8px grid, 12px+ group gaps, no clipping. One clear hero per size, other text 11-14px (never <11px). Believable data.
designSpec: Each of the five concepts renders once: Route Nodes and Night Scrim are Small, Split-Flap Map and Mode Stepper are Medium, and Cobalt Stack is Large. Exact-size tiles use 24px corners, size-appropriate padding, and restrained content; native radar pulsing and static motion cues avoid unsupported animation.
